material_litigation.description: City of Pontiac Reestablished General Employees' Retirement System v. Inspire Medical Systems, Inc., et al. - Securities class action alleging violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act based on purportedly materially false and misleading statements regarding the launch of the Company's Inspire V neurostimulator between August 6, 2024, and August 4, 2025. Voluntarily dismissed on December 23, 2025, and administratively closed on December 29, 2025.

Indiana Public Retirement System v. Inspire Medical Systems, Inc., et al. - Securities class action in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York alleging violations of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and Rule 10b-5, based on purportedly materially false and misleading statements regarding the launch of the Company's Inspire V neurostimulator. Seeks unquantified compensatory damages, attorneys' fees and costs.

Korte v. Herbert, et al. - Stockholder derivative lawsuit filed in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York on behalf of Inspire against certain present and former executive officers and current Board members. Claims include violations of Section 14(a) and Rule 14a-9, Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5, Section 20(a), breach of fiduciary duty, aiding and abetting, unjust enrichment, and waste of corporate assets. Seeks unspecified damages.

Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. v. Nyxoah SA and Nyxoah, Inc. - Patent infringement lawsuit filed in May 2025 in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware alleging that Nyxoah's Genio product infringes certain of Company's U.S. patents related to neurostimulation therapy for obstructive sleep apnea. Seeks judgment of patent infringement and relief including monetary damages such as lost profits. Nyxoah has denied infringement and asserted counterclaims.

Nyxoah, Inc. v. Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. - Patent infringement lawsuit filed in September 2025 in the United States District Court for the District of Delaware alleging that Company's Inspire IV and Inspire V implantable neurostimulators infringe certain of Nyxoah's patents.

Nyxoah SA and Nyxoah, Inc. v. Inspire Medical Systems, Inc. and Inspire Medical Systems Europe GmbH - Patent infringement lawsuit brought in December 2025 in the Unified Patent Court, Munich Division, alleging that Inspire IV implantable neurostimulator infringes a patent owned by Nyxoah.
